name: application-presence-cursor-layer
title: Presence Cursor Layer
description: Overlay of named, colored cursor markers with an optional selection box, showing live collaborator presence over a shared canvas.
useWhen: Building a real-time collaborative surface (design canvas, document, whiteboard) where showing other users' pointer positions builds shared awareness.
You have a live position feed (e.g. from a WebSocket or CRDT presence channel) to drive cursor coordinates.
Users benefit from seeing not just who else is present, but what they're pointing at or selecting.
avoidWhen: You only need to show who is online, not where they are — an `avatar-group` communicates that with far less complexity.
The surface isn't truly real-time collaborative — a static list of collaborators is more honest than simulated cursor positions.
Precise, low-latency positioning matters and you don't have a real transport for position updates — an inaccurate or stale cursor layer is worse than none.
responsiveBehavior: Cursor positions are percentage-based within the canvas container, so they stay correctly placed as the canvas resizes; labels do not reflow and may clip near the canvas edges at very small sizes.
accessibility: The cursor layer is decorative and marked pointer-events-none so it never intercepts clicks meant for the canvas beneath it.
Each cursor has role="img" with an aria-label describing who it belongs to and whether it is selecting a region.
A visually hidden role="status" element announces the current list of active collaborators for screen reader users, since the visual layer alone conveys nothing to them.
Color is paired with a text name label, not used as the only way to distinguish collaborators.

variants.title: Presence Cursor Layer
variants.description: Three collaborator cursors over a shared canvas, one with an active selection box.
accessibility: A screen-reader-only status region lists active collaborators by name, since cursor position is a purely visual signal.

variants.title: Presence Cursor Layer (Dark)
variants.description: Collaborator cursors adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: Cursor label colors are brightened relative to the light variant to hold contrast against the dark canvas.
